scope: Synthetic fixture host tests and execution of its exact extracted pure Kotlin component. No Android device execution is asserted for this source.

behavior.nativeIdentity: Every identity handler reads the same immutable current-host binding. An old queued handler cannot combine its own old host with a new global generation.
behavior.detachedGap: Retained read-only identity handler responds with a coherent detached binding while the retained engine waits for reattachment.
behavior.staleCallbacks: Old UI and cleanup callbacks keep their original generation and cannot change or notify the current host binding.
behavior.mutations: Recreation remains bound to the original exact active host and generation, nonce and report identity. No business or UI mutation is retried.
behavior.consumer: Foreign engine, generation regression and same-generation host conflict remain strict failures, with distinct read-only diagnostics.

dart.interleavedFuture: An old identity Future is held pending while a new-host observation queues. Its delayed hybrid reply fails without tree publication or State change; a coherent current reply publishes the tree once.

coverage: Captured old handler runs after new binding attach
Detached gap returns the same fixed generation and detached visibility
Old display and cleanup cannot change the new binding
Operations on the wrong thread fail without changing state

validation.retainedEarlierAnalysis: The first analysis found one informational closure-style lint in a new test. It was fixed, with the original log retained and final tests/analysis rerun.

boundaries: The exact component JVM test proves component behavior; it does not prove Android lifecycle or Messenger scheduling.
The interleaved Future test proves the Dart asynchronous consumer and does not simulate an Android device.
